summary: A husband can give up some of his rights to his wife's property in writing. The Tanna'im argue about how much he gives up with each wording, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says he cannot give up a right the Torah gives him.

chunks.st: One who writes for his wife in a document the declaration:

chunks.en: I have no claim and no say in your property,
chunks.st: I have no legal dealings or involvement with your property,
chunks.stMore: thereby relinquishing his rights to her possessions,

chunks.en: still eats its fruits while she is alive.
chunks.st: may nevertheless consume the produce of her property in her lifetime.

chunks.en: And if she dies,
chunks.st: And if she dies before him,

chunks.en: I have no claim and no say in your property?
chunks.st: I have no legal dealings or involvement with your property?

chunks.en: So that if she sold it or gave it away,
chunks.st: The result of this declaration is that if she sold or gave away her property,

chunks.en: he does not eat the fruits while she is alive.

chunks.st: but if she dies

chunks.st: I have no legal dealings or involvement with your property

chunks.en: and its fruits, and the fruits of their fruits, while you live and after you die,
chunks.st: or with its produce, or with the produce of its produce, in your lifetime and after your death,

chunks.en: And if she dies,
chunks.st: And if she dies,

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.st: If she dies,

chunks.he: יִירָשֶׁנָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִתְנָה עַל מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה,
chunks.en: he inherits her, because he made a condition against what is written in the Torah,
chunks.st: he does inherit from her, because he stipulates counter to that which is written in the Torah.
chunks.stMore: According to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, a husband inherits from his wife by Torah law,

chunks.st: and whoever stipulates counter to that which is written in the Torah,

summary: A man died, and his wife, a lender and his heirs all want his money. Rabbi Tarfon says to give it to the weakest of them, and Rabbi Akiva says we do not decide a din by mercy, so it goes to the heirs.

chunks.en: One who died and left a wife,
chunks.st: one who died and left behind a wife,

chunks.en: and a lender, and heirs,
chunks.st: and a creditor to whom he owed money, and heirs, all of whom claim payment from his property,

chunks.en: and he had something left for safekeeping or
chunks.st: and he had a deposit or

chunks.en: a loan in the hands of others,
chunks.st: a loan in the possession of others,

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: it is given to the weakest of them.
chunks.st: The deposit or the loan will be given to the weakest one of them, i.e., the one most in need of the money.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: We do not use mercy in a din.
chunks.st: One is not merciful in judgment.
chunks.stMore: If the halakha is that it belongs to one party, one follows the halakha and leaves aside considerations of mercy.

chunks.en: Rather, it is given to the heirs,
chunks.st: Rather, the halakha is that the money will be given to the heirs,

chunks.en: because all the others need to swear, and do not
chunks.st: as all people who wish to exact payment from orphans require an oath before they collect their debt, but

chunks.en: the heirs do not need to swear.
chunks.st: the heirs do not require an oath.
chunks.stMore: They therefore have a more absolute right than the others to their father’s property.

summary: If a man left picked fruit, whoever grabs it first gets it. If the wife or the lender grabbed more than they were owed, Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva argue about the extra.

chunks.en: If he left fruit picked from the ground,
chunks.st: left behind produce that was detached from the ground,

chunks.en: whoever gets them first owns them.
chunks.st: whoever first took possession of them as compensation for what was owed, whether the creditor, the wife, or the heirs, acquired the produce.

chunks.en: If the wife got more than her kesubah,
chunks.st: If the wife acquired this produce and it was worth more than the payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: or the lender more than his loan,
chunks.st: or the creditor acquired this produce and it was worth more than the value of his debt,

chunks.en: the extra: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: what should be done with the surplus? Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: it is given to the weakest of them.
chunks.st: It will be given to the weakest one of them,
chunks.stMore: either the creditor or the wife, depending on the circumstances.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: We do not use mercy in a din.
chunks.st: One is not merciful in judgment.

chunks.en: Rather, it is given to the heirs,
chunks.st: Rather, it will be given to the heirs,

chunks.en: because all the others need to swear, and do not
chunks.st: as all people who wish to exact payment from orphans require an oath before they collect their debt, but

chunks.en: the heirs do not need to swear.
chunks.st: the heirs do not require an oath.

summary: A man who puts his wife in charge of his store or his property may make her swear that she took nothing, whenever he wants. Rabbi Eliezer says even about her spinning and her dough.

chunks.en: One who sets up his wife as a storekeeper
chunks.st: one who establishes his wife as a storekeeper in his store,

chunks.en: or made her a manager,
chunks.st: or if he appointed her as a steward to handle his property and workers,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה מַשְׁבִּיעָהּ כָּל זְמָן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה.
chunks.en: he can make her swear whenever he wants.
chunks.st: this one, i.e., the husband, can administer an oath to her, having her state that she did not appropriate any of his possessions, whenever he wants.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: even about her spindle and her dough.
chunks.st: He can administer an oath even with regard to the products of her spindle and for her dough,
chunks.stMore: which are matters related to the household, and not her function as a storekeeper.

summary: A husband can write that he will not make his wife swear. The mishnah shows how far this goes, to her heirs and to his heirs, depending on the exact words he wrote.

chunks.en: If he wrote to her,
chunks.st: one wrote to his wife in the marriage contract:

chunks.en: I have no vow or oath on you,
chunks.st: I do not have the right to administer a vow or an oath upon you,

chunks.en: he cannot make her swear,
chunks.st: he cannot administer an oath to her.

chunks.en: but he can make swear
chunks.st: However, he can administer an oath to

chunks.en: her heirs and those who come in her place.
chunks.st: her heirs, and to those who come on her authority,
chunks.stMore: either as her representatives or because they purchased her marriage contract.

chunks.en: If he wrote, I have no vow or oath on you,
chunks.st: If the husband wrote: I do not have the right to administer a vow or an oath upon you,

chunks.en: or on your heirs, or on those who come in your place,
chunks.st: or upon your heirs, or upon those who come on your authority,

chunks.en: he cannot make them swear,
chunks.st: he cannot administer an oath to her;

chunks.en: not her and not her heirs
chunks.st: not to her, nor her heirs,

chunks.en: and not those who come in her place.
chunks.st: nor those who come on her authority.

chunks.en: But his heirs can make her swear,
chunks.st: But the husband’s heirs can administer an oath to her,

chunks.en: and her heirs, and those who come in her place.
chunks.st: and to her heirs, and to those who come on her authority.

chunks.en: If he wrote, I have no vow or oath, and not
chunks.st: If he wrote: Neither I,

chunks.st: nor my heirs, nor those who come on my authority have the right to administer a vow or an oath upon you,

chunks.en: or on your heirs, or on those who come in your place,
chunks.st: or upon your heirs, or upon those who come on your authority,

chunks.st: he cannot administer an oath to her or to them;

chunks.en: not he and not his heirs

summary: A widow whose husband freed her from oaths does not have to swear to the heirs if she did not handle his property. If she did handle it, they may make her swear only about what happened after he died.
stIntro: If a woman who was exempted from an oath by her husband

chunks.en: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house,
chunks.st: went from her husband’s grave, immediately after her husband’s death, to her father’s house, without handling her late husband’s property,

chunks.en: or she went back to her father-in-law's house,
chunks.st: or in a case where she returned to her father-in-law’s house

chunks.en: and did not become a manager,
chunks.st: and did not become a steward
chunks.stMore: over the property at all throughout this period,

chunks.en: the heirs cannot make her swear.
chunks.st: then the heirs cannot administer an oath to her
chunks.stMore: with regard to her actions in their father’s lifetime, as the husband exempted her from an oath to the heirs.

chunks.en: But if she became a manager,
chunks.st: And if she became a steward,

chunks.he: הַיּוֹרְשִׁין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
chunks.en: the heirs make her swear about what will happen from now on,
chunks.st: the heirs may administer an oath to her about the future,
chunks.stMore: i.e., anything she did with the property after the death of her husband,

chunks.he: וְאֵין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבָר:
chunks.en: and they do not make her swear about what already happened.
chunks.st: but they cannot administer an oath to her with regard to what took place in the past, during her husband’s lifetime.

summary: Sometimes a woman must swear before she can collect her kesubah. The mishnah lists these cases.

chunks.en: A woman who lowers her kesubah
chunks.explain: She says part of it was paid already.
chunks.st: who vitiates her marriage contract
chunks.stMore: by acknowledging that she has received partial payment

chunks.en: can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: can collect the rest of her marriage contract only by means of an oath.

chunks.en: If one witness says it was paid,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one witness testifies that her marriage contract is paid,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.

chunks.he: מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים וּמִנְּכָסִים מְשֻׁעְבָּדִין וְשֶׁלֹּא בְפָנָיו,
chunks.en: From orphans' property, from property already sold, or when he is not there,
chunks.st: In any case where she seeks to claim her marriage contract from the property of orphans, or from liened property that has been sold to a third party, or when not in her husband’s presence,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.

summary: The mishnah explains each case where a woman swears before she collects her kesubah. Rabbi Shimon says the heirs make her swear whenever she asks for her kesubah.
stIntro: The mishna elaborates: With regard to a woman

chunks.en: How does a woman lower her kesubah?
chunks.st: who vitiates her marriage contract, how so, how does this situation arise?

chunks.en: Her kesubah was a thousand zuz,
chunks.st: If her marriage contract was a thousand dinars,

chunks.en: and he told her, You got your kesubah,
chunks.st: and her husband said to her: You already received your marriage contract,

chunks.he: וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי אֶלָּא מָנֶה,
chunks.en: and she says, I got only one hundred,
chunks.st: and she says: I received only one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she has made a partial admission and can collect her marriage contract only by means of an oath.

chunks.he: עֵד אֶחָד מְעִידָהּ שֶׁהִיא פְרוּעָה כֵּיצַד,
chunks.en: How is it when one witness says it was paid?
chunks.st: If one witness testifies that her marriage contract is paid, how so?

chunks.en: Her kesubah was a thousand zuz,
chunks.st: If her marriage contract was a thousand dinars,

chunks.en: and he told her, You got your kesubah,
chunks.st: and her husband said to her: You already received your marriage contract,

chunks.en: and she says, I did not get it,
chunks.st: and she says: I did not receive payment,

chunks.en: and one witness says it was paid,
chunks.st: and one witness testifies about the marriage contract that it is paid,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.

chunks.en: How is it with property that was sold?
chunks.st: From liened property, how so?

chunks.en: He sold his property to others,
chunks.st: If while they were married the husband sold his property to others,

chunks.en: and she collects from the buyers,
chunks.st: and she comes to collect her marriage contract from the purchasers,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.
chunks.stMore: She may seize property from the purchasers because her husband’s obligation undertaken in the marriage contract predates his obligation in the document of sale.

chunks.en: How is it with orphans' property?
chunks.st: From the property of orphans, how so?

chunks.en: He died and left his property to the orphans,
chunks.st: If the husband died and left his property to orphans,

chunks.en: and she collects from the orphans,
chunks.st: and she comes to collect her marriage contract from the orphans,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.

chunks.en: How is it when he is not there?
chunks.st: Or when not in his presence, how so?

chunks.en: He went away across the sea,
chunks.st: If he went to a country overseas and sent her a bill of divorce, so that

chunks.en: and she collects when he is not there,
chunks.st: she collects her marriage contract when not in his presence,

chunks.en: she can only collect with an oath.
chunks.st: she can collect it only by means of an oath.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Whenever she asks for her kesubah,
chunks.st: Whenever she claims payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: the heirs make her swear.
chunks.st: the heirs administer an oath to her.

chunks.en: And if she does not ask for her kesubah,
chunks.st: And if she does not claim payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: the heirs do not make her swear.
chunks.st: the heirs do not administer an oath to her.

summary: A woman with a get can collect her kesubah, but a lost get or a missing prosbul is a problem, except in times of danger. The mishnah also teaches how many kesubos a woman collects, and that some kesubos written earlier still count.
stIntro: In a case where a woman

chunks.en: If she brought out a get without a kesubah with it,
chunks.st: produced a bill of divorce and it was unaccompanied by a marriage contract,
chunks.stMore: and she demands that her husband pay her marriage contract,

chunks.en: she collects her kesubah.
chunks.st: she collects payment of her marriage contract, and he cannot claim that he already paid it.

chunks.en: A kesubah without a get with it,
chunks.st: If she produced a marriage contract, and it was unaccompanied by a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: she says, My get was lost,
chunks.st: and she says: My bill of divorce was lost,

chunks.en: and he says, My receipt was lost;
chunks.st: and he says: Just as your bill of divorce was lost, so too my receipt for the payment of your marriage contract was lost;

chunks.en: and so a lender who brought out a document of
chunks.st: and likewise, in a case of a creditor who produced a promissory note after the Sabbatical Year,

chunks.en: a loan without a prosbul with it,

chunks.en: these are not paid.
chunks.st: and demanded payment of the debt, these debts may not be collected.

chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: From the time of danger and on,

chunks.st: From the time of danger and onward,

chunks.en: a woman collects her kesubah without a get,
chunks.st: a woman collects payment of her marriage contract without a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: and a lender collects without a prosbul.
chunks.st: and a creditor collects debts owed to him without a prosbol.

chunks.en: Two gittin and two kesubos:
chunks.st: If a woman had two bills of divorce and two marriage contracts
chunks.stMore: as a result of her divorce and remarriage to the same man, the fact that she is in possession of these documents proves that she was never paid for her first marriage contract, and she

chunks.en: she collects two kesubos.
chunks.st: collects two marriage contracts.

chunks.en: Two kesubos and one get,
chunks.st: If she was in possession of two marriage contracts and only one bill of divorce;

chunks.en: or a kesubah and two gittin,
chunks.st: or if she had one marriage contract and two bills of divorce;

chunks.en: or a kesubah, a get, and his death,
chunks.st: or if she had a marriage contract, a bill of divorce, and witnesses to her husband’s death after their remarriage,

chunks.en: she collects only one kesubah.
chunks.st: she collects payment of only one marriage contract.

chunks.en: Because one who divorces his wife and takes her back
chunks.st: This is because there is a presumption that one who divorces his wife and remarries her,

chunks.en: takes her back with the first kesubah.
chunks.st: remarries her with the intention of using her first marriage contract,
chunks.stMore: and she agrees that she collects payment of only the original document. This is the presumption, unless he wrote another marriage contract for her.

chunks.en: A young boy whose father married him off:
chunks.st: In the case of a minor who was married off by his father,

chunks.en: her kesubah still counts,
chunks.st: the wife’s marriage contract that the minor wrote is valid
chunks.stMore: even after the husband comes of age. He cannot excuse himself by saying that it was drafted when he was a minor,

chunks.en: because with this he kept her.
chunks.st: as it is on this condition, the terms of this marriage contract, that he maintained her as his wife upon his maturity.

chunks.en: A man who became a ger together with his wife:
chunks.st: Similarly, in the case of a convert whose wife converted with him,

chunks.en: her kesubah still counts,
chunks.st: the marriage contract that she had as a gentile is valid,

chunks.en: because with this he kept her.
chunks.st: for on this condition he maintained her as his wife.
